title: Case, senior product manager, weak answers

questions.text: GatePass sells event tickets. Ticket volume grew 20 percent this year, but fee revenue is flat. Leadership wants a plan. How do you start?
Finance suggests raising fees, product suggests parking add-ons, and sales suggests more venues. You have one team this half. How do you choose?
Estimate the yearly fee revenue GatePass could earn from parking add-ons in one large city.
How would you measure whether a fee change hurt customer trust?
A large venue threatens to leave over fees. What do you do?
How would you set the goal for GatePass next year?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Gwen, I'm Peter, a director of product. This is a thirty minute case interview, spoken only.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Peter, thanks for having me.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How has your week been?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Fine, a bit tiring. I have had many meetings.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: I will ask three cases. They are open, so use your own judgment, and ask questions if you need more context.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: GatePass sells event tickets. Ticket volume grew 20 percent this year, but fee revenue is flat. Leadership wants a plan. How do you start?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would look at the fees. Maybe the fees are too low. We could raise them a little and then revenue goes up.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Volume grew 20 percent. What could explain flat revenue?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Maybe people are buying cheaper tickets. Or there are more discounts. I am not sure. I would ask the data team.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What would you ask the data team for first?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would ask for revenue per ticket by price band and by event type. Then I can see whether cheap events are growing faster than big ones.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Finance suggests raising fees, product suggests parking add-ons, and sales suggests more venues. You have one team this half. How do you choose?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think all three are good. Raising fees is fast. Add-ons are good for customers. More venues is also growth. I would try to do all of them over time.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: You only have one team this half. Which one first?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Add-ons first, because customers get something and not only a higher price. Fees can upset customers and make them leave. Venues take a long time.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Estimate the yearly fee revenue GatePass could earn from parking add-ons in one large city.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A large city has many events. Many people drive, so many would buy parking. If parking costs some money, the revenue would be big.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Can you put numbers on that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Maybe a million tickets. Maybe a lot buy parking. So the revenue is a few million dollars, I guess.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What are the main goals for the product team this year?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Grow revenue per ticket and keep the customer trust score above its current level.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is our time, Gwen. The recruiter will follow up within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Peter.

notes: Weak for senior: generic answers, no structure, no numbers in the estimate, no ranked recommendation.
